title: Largest sum without neighbours
summary: Return the largest sum of elements of `values` that can be chosen without taking two that are next to each other.
hints: Look at the last element. Either you take it or you do not. What does each choice leave you free to do with the rest?
If you take element i you cannot take i - 1, so you add its value to the best answer for the first i - 2 elements. If you skip it, you keep the best answer for the first i - 1 elements.
best[i] = max(best[i - 1], best[i - 2] + values[i]). You only ever need the previous two results, so two variables are enough.
pattern: Dynamic programming: take it or skip it
takeaway: Many optimisation problems reduce to one decision per element, with the best earlier results reused. Always picking the larger neighbour (a greedy choice) fails; [2, 1, 1, 2] is the counter-example.
